requirements.note: Inset-grouped History, newest first, in month sections; each row shows name, date, exercise count and volume (e.g. 6,767.5 lb). A new workout appears at the top.
The detail screen has a Date/Exercises/Sets/Total Volume summary, then one card per exercise with its muscle·equipment and numbered sets; the exercise row pushes to the exercise screen.

Start from the Workout tab or the + button; an empty name falls back to 'Workout' and can be renamed inline. The picker sheet has a bottom search bar and a Muscle pull-down menu, both working together; you can pick several exercises ('Add 2'). The Add Set sheet uses a decimal pad and pre-fills from the last set. Tapping a set opens Edit, which has Delete Set. Finish is disabled until a set is logged, then saves to History. There is no swipe-to-delete on sets.
The Exercises tab lists all exercises grouped by muscle, with equipment as the subtitle and push to detail. The tab itself has no search.
Best Set card (72.5 lb, 14 reps, with date), Muscle/Equipment, and 'Workouts (4)' rows with top weight per workout. A newly finished workout is included.
An in-progress workout (name, exercises, sets) survived relaunch; the History + button turns into 'Current Workout'. A finished workout survived relaunch.

bugs: After a horizontal swipe on a set row in the current workout, the next tap on set or exercise rows is swallowed: nothing happens until a second tap or some other interaction. Once the rows briefly vanished from the accessibility tree.
No limit on weight: a typo like 98135.5 lb is accepted and logged.
tells: No swipe-to-delete on set rows. Deleting needs a tap into the edit sheet, where a hand-built UIKit/SwiftUI list would offer a trailing swipe action.
The Workout and exercise screens show an opaque white nav-bar band over the grouped grey background at rest, with a hard edge, where iOS 26+ is transparent until scrolled.
The current workout shows its name twice: as the large title and again in a text field right below it.
The Start Workout row has no disabled or button styling and starts with an empty name, silently using 'Workout'.
The picker list isn't alphabetical (it appears in id order), unlike the alphabetical library tab.
A.scroll: History scrolls smoothly with native momentum, the large title collapses with the iOS 26 soft scroll-edge blur, and there are no blank or popping rows. Scroll position is kept when returning from a detail push.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped History, newest first, in month sections; each row has a bold name, the date, and 'N exercises · volume' on a third line. Rows are tall (98 pt) but correct.
The detail screen has a Date/Exercises/Sets/Total Volume summary, then one section per exercise with a tinted header that pushes to the exercise, numbered sets, and a per-exercise volume footer.

The New Workout form has a name field, name suggestions, and Start disabled while the name is empty. The picker has a search field and horizontal muscle filter chips, multi-select with checkmarks, and 'Add (2)'. The Add Set sheet has steppers plus a decimal pad, a keyboard-accessory Add button, a live volume readout, and pre-fills from the last set. Tapping a set opens Edit with Delete Set, and swipe-to-delete works. However, tapping Finish crashes the app every time (reproduced twice). The workout does land in History after relaunch.
The Library tab is grouped by muscle with counts ('Arms (20)') and equipment subtitles, and pushes to detail. The tab itself has no search.
Muscle/Equipment, a large Best Set card (72.5 lb, 14 reps, the workout and date, tappable), and '4 Workouts' rows listing every set and the top weight.
An in-progress workout survived relaunch and the app reopened on the Workout tab, which carries a badge. History persisted, including the workouts saved just before the crashes.

bugs: Tapping Finish on a workout in progress crashes the app to the Home Screen, reproduced 2 out of 2 times. The data is saved, but the user sees a crash at the most important moment.
On the exercise screen, the first 'Workouts' row stays shown as selected (grey highlight) after arriving from a workout detail and doesn't clear.
On the New Workout form, the Start Workout button sits under the keyboard while you type the name and the list doesn't scroll it into view (Return does start the workout).
tells: The stuck grey selection highlight on a list row is not how a system list deselects.
History rows are three lines tall, so the list runs to 11 screens for 60 workouts, less dense than a typical iOS log.
The History screen has no toolbar + button; a workout can only be started from the Workout tab.
B.scroll: Smooth native scrolling with momentum and scroll-edge blur under the collapsed title, no blank or popping rows, and position kept on returning from detail. The tall rows make the list long.

why: Both apps look and scroll like native iOS 26 apps, and B has the richer set entry (steppers, swipe-to-delete, suggestions). But B crashes every time you tap Finish, the moment the whole app is built around. A completes every flow without crashing; its flaws are smaller ones, like no swipe-to-delete, a swallowed tap after a swipe, and an opaque nav-bar band.
